tools.name: place_call
tools.description: Use this when the user needs something from a US or Canadian business that takes a phone call: book, cancel, get prices or availability, check an order or whether a repair is done, reach a person or wait on hold, ask for an upgrade, ask an office how to do something, or ask a vendor if they're free

tools.name: wait_for_setup
tools.description: After place_call returned needs_setup and the user has SEEN the link: wait for them to finish it. If your client only shows your reply when your turn ends (ChatGPT), end your turn with the link first and call this after the user replies. Returns as soon as they're done and places the call right then

tools.name: get_call
tools.description: Follow a call you placed: status, the business's pending question, answers, a live transcript, and the final outcome. Waits up to wait_seconds (max 50; use 45) and returns early when you need to act: the business asks something, an answer is recorded, or the call ends with its outcome. Loop until st

tools.name: answer_question
tools.description: Send a message into a live call; the assistant says it within a couple of seconds. Use it to answer pending_question (pass its question_id; the business is waiting, about 45 seconds), or anytime to change course: "Make it 6 people instead of 4", "Also ask if they price-match", "Don't book, just get

tools.name: hang_up
tools.description: End a live call now. Use when the user asks to stop, or the call is clearly stuck. An answered call is still billed ($1 covers the first 2 minutes; demo lines and unanswered calls are free). Afterwards get_call returns ended_reason "you_hung_up" and a summary of what was learned.

tools.name: redial
tools.description: Call the same business again with the same request, plus any changes: a missing detail, a new question, another day. Use after a call ended busy, unanswered, in voicemail, or with unanswered_questions, or when the user says "call them back and ask...". The assistant is told which phone-menu options

tools.name: share_call
tools.description: Only when the user asks: make a public, read-only page for a finished call (result and transcript) that they can send or post. The user's name, phone numbers and emails are always hidden; the business name is hidden unless show_business=true. public=false turns an existing link off.

tools.name: plan_call
tools.description: Free preview before place_call, no account needed: the opening line, what the business will probably ask that you haven't provided (get it from the user BEFORE calling; every gap becomes a live question the business waits on), whether the business is open now, tips (best time to call, when to use tr

tools.name: call_around
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to compare several businesses of a kind or find one that can help: it finds them near a place and calls them with the same goal, from 1 to 100. Examples: "call 3 mechanics near Plano, TX for front brake prices", "ask every pharmacy near 75024 when they close", "call hair

tools.name: get_batch
tools.description: Progress of a call_around batch: totals, a results table (business, status, success, summary, price, times, answers), every question a business is waiting on (answer each with answer_question right away), and spend. wait_seconds (up to 50) waits for something to change. Without batch_id it returns t

tools.name: stop_batch
tools.description: Stop dialing new places in a batch (e.g. the user already got what they needed). Calls in progress finish unless hang_up_active=true.

tools.name: find_business
tools.description: Find a US or Canadian business's phone number, address, whether it's open now, today's hours, local time and rating. Pass near (city and state or province, or a zip or postal code); without it results can be anywhere in the US. No account needed. Also finds CallForMe's free fictional demo lines by n

tools.name: list_calls
tools.description: Recent calls on the user's account, newest first, with status, answers and outcome (no transcripts). Use to find a call_id, or for "what did they quote last time?". For one call's live status or transcript, use get_call; for a call_around batch, get_batch. Returns nothing until the account has place

tools.name: account
tools.description: The user's CallForMe balance, auto-reload setting, recent spend and projected run-out date, the "pause calls under" setting, their most recent call, and a link to add credit. Use it when the user asks about their balance, spend or settings, or before a large call_around to check the balance covers i

tools.name: pricing
tools.description: What a call costs (per answered call, per minute after the first 2, the 30-minute cap), what's free (unanswered and busy calls, the demo lines), and how credit and auto-reload work. Read-only; use it when the user asks about cost before a call.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "plan_call" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Free preview before place_call, no account needed: the opening line, what the business will probably ask that you haven't provided (get it from the user BEFORE …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "call_around" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_call, answer_question, share_call, list_calls · Public sink: answer_question, share_call · Destructive: account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_call, answer_question, share_call, list_calls · Public sink: answer_question, share_call · Destructive: account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "place_call" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Place a real phone call to a US or Canadian business. findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
